newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares ease, trade thin on Fed uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares ease, trade thin on Fed uncertainty.

text.p: Leading Russian shares closed down slightly on Tuesday as investors, fearing a rate hike by the U.S. Federal Reserve, sold lightly, traders said.
Trade volume was extremely low, $22.7 million reported on the Russian Trading System, and traders were divided how the market would react to a Fed decision, expected late on Tuesday.
The RTS 23-share index closed fell to 303.33 from Monday's 310.44 close.

National power utility UES EESR.RTS eased to $0.1930 from $0.1985 at Monday's close. Regional power utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS fell to $1.26 from $1.29 and oil producer Surgutneftegaz SNGS.RTS eased to $0.762 from $0.765.

"It was too much for some people's nerves, especially for short term Russian -- and perhaps foreign -- investors," said Alexander Bubnovsky, Alfa Capital's director of trading operations who predicted a rebound however the Fed acted.
Dmitry Yevenko, head of securities at United City Bank, said investors fearing the hike had sold days earlier and the market would react most to if the Fed did not raise rates by 25 basis points.
A market drop was more likely than a rise on Wednesday, he added.
"Many want to face the event (the possible Fed decision) with empty portfolios," he said.
"If what the market is expecting actually happens, it will only have a neutral effect. It will be worse if the decision is unexpected -- the market doesn't like surprises," he said.
Bubnovsky said prices had fallen to support levels and that investors would snap up cheap shares once the tension of the rate question was over.
"People will quickly start buying again if they see prices they like," he said. "At the moment they're still making sure that there aren't any more big sellers left in the market."
